fine_lines.title: talk the talk vs walk the walk
fine_lines.explanation_ar: talk the talk = يتحدث بثقة عن موضوع وكأنه خبير، وقد لا يعرف الكثير فعلاً. walk the walk = يفعل ما يقول فعلاً ويثبت ذلك بالعمل. يُقال: He can talk the talk, but can he walk the walk?
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Talk the talk' = speak confidently about something, but maybe without real knowledge. 'Walk the walk' = actually do what you say. We often say: He can talk the talk, but can he walk the walk?

examples.sentence: He can talk the talk about fitness, but he never exercises.
Our coach really walks the walk – she trains every day.

fine_lines.title: take the biscuit vs just the ticket
fine_lines.explanation_ar: take the biscuit (تعبير سلبي) = تصرف مدهش في سوئه أو إزعاجه، «هذا أسوأ شيء!». just the ticket (تعبير إيجابي) = هذا تماماً ما أحتاجه.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Take the biscuit' is negative: something so annoying or surprising it is the worst. 'Just the ticket' is positive: exactly what you need.

examples.sentence: He was late, and then he asked me to pay – that really takes the biscuit!
A hot bowl of soup is just the ticket on a cold day.

fine_lines.title: bite the bullet vs take the rough with the smooth
words: take the rough with the smooth
fine_lines.explanation_ar: bite the bullet = تقرّر أن تفعل شيئاً صعباً أو مزعجاً لا مفرّ منه. take the rough with the smooth = تقبل الجوانب السيئة في وضعٍ ما مع الجوانب الجيدة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Bite the bullet' = decide to do a difficult or unpleasant thing you can't avoid. 'Take the rough with the smooth' = accept the bad parts of a situation together with the good parts.

examples.sentence: I bit the bullet and went to the dentist.

examples.word: take the rough with the smooth
examples.sentence: Every job has bad days – you take the rough with the smooth.

expressions.example: Come on, spill the tea – why did they leave early?

expressions.meaning_ar: يكون أسوأ أو أغرب تصرف مزعج
expressions.meaning_en: to be the most annoying or surprising thing
expressions.example: He ate my lunch and then complained about it – that takes the biscuit!

expressions.meaning_ar: يُقدِم على أمر صعب أو مزعج لا مفرّ منه
expressions.meaning_en: to make yourself do something difficult or unpleasant
expressions.example: I hate phoning the bank, but I'll have to bite the bullet.

expressions.meaning_ar: يتحدث بثقة كالخبير، وربما لا يعرف كثيراً
expressions.meaning_en: to speak confidently about something, maybe without real knowledge
expressions.example: He can talk the talk, but he has never actually built a website.

expressions.meaning_en: to actually do what you say
expressions.example: Don't just promise to help – walk the walk.

expressions.meaning_ar: ينتظر حتى يهدأ الوضع قبل أن يتصرّف
expressions.meaning_en: to wait for a situation to calm down before doing anything
expressions.example: Let's let the dust settle before we discuss it again.

expressions.meaning_en: exactly what is needed or wanted
expressions.example: A short break is just the ticket after a long drive.

expressions.phrase: take the rough with the smooth
expressions.meaning_en: to accept the bad things in a situation as well as the good things
expressions.example: Living in a big city is exciting and noisy – you take the rough with the smooth.

expressions.meaning_en: more people make an occasion more fun
expressions.example: Can my cousin come too? – Of course, the more the merrier!

expressions.meaning_en: to make someone or something famous or important
expressions.example: The new museum has put our small town on the map.

expressions.meaning_ar: يخفّض ذروة المنحنى (مثلاً عدد الإصابات بمرض) ويوزّعها على وقت أطول
expressions.meaning_en: to reduce the peak of a graph, e.g. the number of people getting ill at the same time

grammar.title: The + comparative, the + comparative
grammar.explanation_ar: نمط the more ..., the merrier يعني «كلما ... كلما ...»: the + صيغة المقارنة، the + صيغة المقارنة. أمثلة: The sooner, the better. The more you practise, the better you speak.
grammar.explanation_en: The pattern 'the + comparative, the + comparative' shows that two things change together: The sooner, the better. The more you practise, the better you speak.
examples: The harder you work, the more you learn.
